reviewer.role: separate reviewer agent requested by controller
reviewer.modelIdentity: Codex/GPT-6 agent family exposed by host; exact provider revision unavailable
reviewer.exposure: Full-history fork with supplied repository/host instructions and delegated task. Author README/REVIEW, manifests, candidate references, selected controller/rubrics/assertion records were read. No subject answers exist in this review. No tuning was performed.
reviewer.captureLimits: Full provider/internal instructions and internal prior context unavailable. Full exact upstream conversation/provider request and automatic truncation boundaries unavailable; no claim of a clean-room or exact full-provider transcript. Visible delegated task and followup preserved verbatim. Tool calls/results remain in host session; selected immutable inputs are hashed here.
reviewer.sourceLimits: No network source verification or model-provider calls. Six captured SDK paths absent; fresh SDK verification unknown. No native code execution, installations, extra agents, external worker messages, Git publication or state/approval changes.

revision.identityBasis: Exact reviewed local file hashes in input-audit.json; checkout contains later commits; no assertion that full tree equals coordinator checkpoint.

comparability.accepted: All 24 paired user request bytes equal their linked subjects; generic references empty. All 48 payload hashes and selected embedded-reference hashes verified. Same shared text-only host boundary; only candidate instruction/reference treatment differs. One operational rubric revision must grade both arms.
comparability.limits: C0 versus C2/C2-sdk/C2-policy or C1 measures bundled context benefit, not instruction-only lift, installed discovery, autonomous retrieval or released skill superiority. Reference asymmetry is deliberate treatment, not neutral-task leakage. Protocol branding/routing must be scored separately and never penalize C0 for absent candidate formatting. Twelve related families, not 48 independent questions; near-duplicate iOS SwiftUI semantics/no-change cases should not inflate uncertainty. No actual harness isolation attestation, provider identity, quota or execution record exists.

leakage.staticReview: No controller rubric/solutions/incident narratives identified in paired neutral requests. Candidate task notes intentionally supply strategies closely aligned to criteria; that is the declared controlled-context treatment. It cannot establish generalization to unseen tasks. Manifest identities/routes are retained controller-side; supplied reference path labels are deliberate provenance.
leakage.runtimeIsolation: unknown; no live subject harness reviewed or executed. Must exclude repository/controller mount, author history and this report in any later session.

oracle.exactMethodAndReceiptPins: verified against current local bytes; input-audit.json contains method hashes, receipt attempts and environments
oracle.positiveAndNegativeScope: Existing saved receipts are provenance, not fresh execution; no positive/mutant fixture was run. Assertion methods and selected negative-control records do not establish generated accessibility behavior. FD-04 actual independent exemplar grading/reconciliation is not completed by conceptual calibration.
oracle.alternativePolicy: Semantic task success, not exact implementation or fixture shape. Blocking action interpretation and source bindings require adjudication before full-package acceptance.

findings.evidence: The prompt asks that callbacks stay attached to the current file. The rubric fail rule says: Old action reaches a rebound file, or the disabled shortcut still acts. Linked fixtures reject retained per-binding actions using revisions. The supplied action note also describes current-item operation, so it does not exclude a stable dispatcher.
findings.impact: A supported single installed handler that reads the owner’s current file and enabled state on activation can satisfy the developer task without per-binding invalidation. A blanket retained-action rejection can falsely fail this alternative. No subject response has yet exhibited this failure.
findings.requiredDisposition: Before grading, define stale invocation versus stable current-owner dispatch in an additive controller clarification shared by both arms. Accept the stable dispatcher when the task gives no per-binding delayed-operation contract; require rejection for callbacks actually owned by an obsolete file/request. Alternatively revise the subject task in a new package if strict retained-per-binding rejection is intended. Preserve sealed v2.
findings.acceptedAlternative: Install an action once; on activation resolve the current owner/file and enabled policy, dispatch once; detach at teardown. No append-on-update and no obsolete captured owner.

findings.evidence: V2 correctly replaces five iOS-scoped guides with narrow SDK cards and replaces two testing contexts, but frozen operational rubric sources still name the old guides. In particular macos-appkit-testing sources quote a mandatory three-part manual workflow and tvos-swiftui-testing cites lists/forms.
findings.impact: Unchanged rubric bytes preserve comparison identity but do not themselves provide v2-applicable criterion-level sources. The package resolution narrative is an overlay lead, not a fresh primary-source check or independent binding of every criterion.
findings.requiredDisposition: Use a separately hashed controller source-applicability overlay mapping the v2 cards/project policy to the exact affected criteria and explicitly demoting superseded anchors to historical context. Do not edit the sealed payloads or claim full guide behavior from declaration cards.

findings.evidence: All six captured SDK declaration paths are absent on this Linux reviewer host. Captured excerpts and local hashes agree internally; source SDK files cannot be freshly re-read here.
findings.impact: Enclosing @available annotations are correctly distinguished from module migration annotations in the captured text. Original declaration authenticity/currency remains unknown in this review; no API nonavailability is inferred.
findings.requiredDisposition: Retain unknown verification status. Existing signed-off external declaration verification, if later obtained, must be a separate recorded evidence step; no native rerun or lookup is requested by this report.

findings.evidence: iOS SwiftUI media assertions cover unavailable/empty lists, request ordering and synthetic selection plus mute/volume; they do not cover errors, actual player replacement or selected AVMediaSelection preservation. Mac SwiftUI state links media/form snapshot units rather than a complete card. TV SwiftUI action criterion-1 links stale-item rejection but not disabled dispatch.
findings.impact: These are partial cross-context policy observations, not a complete executable answer oracle. The existing missing/scope language generally acknowledges this correctly.
findings.requiredDisposition: Keep these criteria answer/source-reviewed. Do not convert linked fixture passes into whole-criterion passes or subject compilation claims; accept equivalent typed state/ownership designs. Additional native execution is outside this review.

findings.evidence: The tasks permit stated assumptions and design answers without existing source. Mac text cards explicitly do not establish a system size-setting source; grouping/rotors are optional; lifecycle origin may disappear.
findings.impact: Graders must not demand automatic macOS system settings propagation, literal Pay object identity in a hypothetical SwiftUI value view, a rotor, a fixed fallback ID, an adaptive stack axis, or a particular token spelling. Reentrancy ordering is required only when an answer exposes reentrant external work; serialized/no-reentry alternatives can satisfy the same invariant.
findings.requiredDisposition: Apply the accepted interpretations below consistently to both arms. Unsupported exact API claims remain insufficient evidence, while a bounded conditional integration can be valid.
